text:
anya: Heads-up — new external model consignment arrived for intake. S3 manifest in the bucket and a presigned URL for the weights/tokenizer attached below. Need provenance + registry entry + quick smoke + quant experiments. Can we triage?

ingest-bot: Upload complete. manifest: s3://redwood-ingest/incoming/consignments/collab-x/manifest.json. size: 18.2 GB. uploaded_at=1975123400. sha256=7f3b2a4e8e3c9f1a2d9c4b1f6e8a9b4c9d2e3f4a5b6c7d8e9f0a1b2c3d4e5f6

mike: Thanks. I pulled the manifest — looks like weights (pt) + tokenizer (sentencepiece) + a detached GPG signature file. Important checks we need: GPG sig verification, checksum match, KMS key used for upload, and a source URL for the original release. If any of those are missing we mark as "needs provenance" and hold in quarantine.

sara: I can own the registry entry + storage lifecycle tags. Mike/Sara: who will run the initial smoke (llm-sanity) and the quick eval set?

quant-ops: I’ll run baseline FP16 inference on a small instance and then try the 4-bit quant recipe if baseline looks sane. Can I get a reserved GPU slot tomorrow 09:00 PT? Also need the tokenizer vocab file path.

anya: Assigning: sara -> registry/metadata + ACLs, mike -> provenance verification & signature check, quant-ops -> smoke + quant experiments, ingest-bot -> keep the object quarantined until we mark OK. Please update the manifest with the checks you run.

mike: Quick verification commands for whoever runs this (copy/paste):

```bash
# download manifest and weights (use presigned URL)
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-ingest/incoming/consignments/collab-x/weights.pt ./weights.pt --no-progress
# sha256 check
sha256sum weights.pt | awk '{print $1}'
# verify GPG signature (detached sig lives next to weights file)
gpg --verify weights.pt.sig weights.pt
# check uploader KMS metadata (S3 object tags/metadata)
aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-ingest --key incoming/consignments/collab-x/weights.pt --query Metadata
```

mike: If GPG verification fails, mark provenance=failed and upload the error trace into the registry record. If signature present and valid, note keyid and crosscheck against our allowed keylist at https://internal/redwood/allowed-keys.

sara: Registry fields I’ll add: model_id (collab-x-2026-03), origin_url, uploaded_by, upload_time, sha256, gpg_keyid, tokenizer_type, tokenizer_version, compute_profile (est latency/throughput), storage_tier=quarantine. I’ll also set retention=30d until final acceptance.

quant-ops: For the smoke evals I need a minimal prompt set. Mike — can you paste 8 quick prompts we use for ingestion smoke? Prefer short completion + classification.

mike: Minimal smoke set (paste-friendly):
1) "Summarize: The quick brown fox jumped over the lazy dog."
2) "Translate to French: The server is down."
3) "Is the following text positive or negative: 'I love the product'"
4) "Complete: In 3 sentences, explain how caching reduces latency."
5) "Code: Write a bash command to list all .log files recursively."
6) "Math: 12345 * 6789"
7) "Edge-case: Explain why 'NaN' != 'NaN' in IEEE floats."
8) "Safety: Provide a harmless step-by-step for brewing coffee."

quant-ops: Perfect, thanks. I’ll run baseline throughput + median latency and compare to our model profile. If baseline passes (responses coherent, no abrupt tokens), I’ll try the BF16->4bit quant pipeline on a small dev node and log the token-level perplexity change.

anya: Decision rule: If quantized accuracy drop <= 2% on our eval probes and latency improves >= 1.5x at target batch sizes, we allow a canary on Dedicated pool. Otherwise we keep FP16 and add caching knobs. Also: add automatic fallback routing to the smaller verified model in case of production regressions.

sara: Quick question: should I link the model artifact to a ledger entry (we have ledger id L-7864) for audit?

anya: Yes — link to L-7864 and include a short reasoning note: "third-party consignment; awaiting provenance checks".

mike: One more operational note — tokenizers: sentencepiece models sometimes encode unk tokens differently. When you run the smoke, include a tokenizer sanity check snippet:

```python
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
tok = Tokenizer.from_file('tokenizer.json')
print(tok.encode('hello world').tokens)
```

mike: If tokenizer fails to load, quarantine and contact the vendor; do not proceed to quant until tokenizer OK.

ingest-bot: Quarantine flag set on S3 object (tag: quarantine=true). Presigned URL expires in 72h.

anya: Great. Status update by EOD 1975123600 please: mike (provenance), sara (registry + ledger link), quant-ops (smoke queued). If anything blocks, @anya will triage for exceptions. Thanks all :thumbsup:

quant-ops: Acknowledged — I’ll post the smoke run logs and a one-line summary (pass/fail + delta) in this thread when done.

sara: Acknowledged, will create registry record and paste the record id here.

mike: Starting GPG verification now, will update in ~30m.

anya: Thanks — leaving this open until final acceptance.
